analysis.title: SiTime Corp. (SITM): Datacenter and idiosyncratic smartphone wins continue to ramp as estimates move higher
key_insights: GS expects SITM to trade higher after the 3Q26 print and 4Q guidance. Buy rating reiterated. GS sees upside to Street estimates in 2027 and beyond.
3Q26 revenue was $299 mn, vs GS $302 mn and Street $288 mn. Non-GAAP gross margin was 70.7% vs GS and Street at 68.0%. Non-GAAP EPS was $4.01 vs GS $3.86 and Street $3.55.

The Communications, Enterprise & Datacenter segment (includes Datacenter) printed $127 mn, below GS at $142 mn and the Street at $146 mn. GS says the stronger outlook for this segment and upside in Consumer & Mobile should give better-than-normal seasonality into 1H27.

IoT, Consumer & Mobile revenue was $50 mn vs GS $42 mn and Street $44 mn. Auto, Industrial & Aerospace was $36 mn vs GS $31 mn and Street $36 mn. Revenue from the acquired Renesas Timing portfolio (TPD) was $86 mn vs GS $87 mn and Street $85 mn.

Management cited a higher book-bill ratio in 3Q and a growing order funnel for 2027 and 2028: $1.4 bn in industrial, close to $1 bn in automotive and $900 mn in aerospace & defense. It also flagged an additional $4 bn opportunity in semiconductor co-packaging, most of it ramping in 2028 and 2029.
Management expects datacenter content gains and volume trends at Apple for internal modem devices to offset typical 1Q27 seasonal weakness.

Wafer constraints are expected to last through 2027. The most severe issues are in the TPD segment, which is growing much faster than expected, and management expects them to be addressed by 1Q27. Core SiTime supply constraints are described as manageable and expected to improve by the start of 1Q27.

Non-GAAP gross margin was 70.7% in 3Q and is guided to about 70% in 4Q, on better product mix, the TPD addition (margins above corporate average) and better manufacturing absorption. Management expects margin to stay in the 70% range, plus or minus one point.
SiTime announced a 3:1 stock split effective December 7, 2026. Management will keep investing in R&D engineering capacity and go-to-market as TPD integration continues.

4Q26 guidance at the midpoint: revenue $336 mn (GS $315 mn, Street $310 mn), non-GAAP gross margin 70% (GS 67.0%, Street 67.5%), non-GAAP EPS $4.76 (GS $3.62, Street $3.67). Non-GAAP OpEx is guided flat sequentially.

GS raised CY26/27/28 EPS estimates by about 9% on average. The 12-month price target was cut to $800 from $900 on a 48x multiple (from 60x, on lower peer multiples) applied to normalized EPS of $16.75 (from $15.00).

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $800 from $900 as the multiple falls to 48x from 60x on lower peer multiples, partly offset by normalized EPS rising to $16.75. Implies 98.4% upside from $403.27.

sector_views.rationale: GS cites the secular shift from quartz to silicon timing, with added tailwinds from AI and datacenter content and a growing Apple opportunity.

earnings_insights: SITM 3Q26 (reported 11/4): revenue $299 mn vs GS est $302 mn and Visible Alpha Street consensus $288 mn. Non-GAAP (excl. SBC) EPS $4.01 vs GS est $3.86 and Street $3.55. Non-GAAP gross margin 70.7% vs GS and Street at 68.0%.

SITM 4Q26 guidance (midpoint): revenue $336 mn (range $331-341 mn) vs GS est $315 mn and Street $310 mn. Non-GAAP EPS $4.76 vs GS est $3.62 and Street $3.67. Non-GAAP gross margin 70.0% (range 69-71%) vs GS est 67.0% and Street 67.5%.
GS segment estimate changes: IoT, Consumer & Mobile 2027E revenue raised 48.7% to $205 mn. Communications, Enterprise & Datacenter 2028E revenue cut 6.2% to $788 mn.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SITM, 12-month price target $800 (48x normalized EPS of $16.75)
trade_ideas.rationale: Growth momentum from datacenter content, Apple internal modem volumes and quartz-to-silicon timing, with Street under-modeling EPS.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower AI datacenter spending, and weaker design win momentum at key datacenter or smartphone customers.
